questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 4515 × 5 – 431 ÷ 3 + 821 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs the expression becomes 4515 ÷ 5 + 431 × 3 − 821 = 903 + 1293 − 821 = 1375.

questions.text: 31 is related to 152 by certain logic. Following the same logic, 47 is related to 168. To which of the following is 66 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is related to the number 121 more than it: 31 + 121 = 152 and 47 + 121 = 168, so 66 + 121 = 187.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. In three of the four pairs, the same pattern is applied and hence they form a group. Select the number-pair that DOES NOT belong to this group. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 335 - 119, 317 - 101 and 308 - 92 the second number is 216 less than the first. 358 − 216 = 142, not 152, so 358 - 152 is the odd one.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'NAME’ is written as 'FNBO' and 'NANO' is written as 'POBO’. How will 'NAIL’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is written in reverse and every letter moves one step forward: NAME → EMAN → FNBO, NANO → ONAN → POBO. So NAIL → LIAN → MJBO.

questions.text: The question contains pairs of words that are related to each other in a certain way. Three of the following four word pairs are alike as these have the same relationship and thus form a group. Which word pair is the one that DOES NOT belong to that group? (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.)
questions.explanation: Each pair names a shape and its number of sides. A hexagon has 6 sides, not 8, so 'Hexagon - 8 sides' does not belong.

questions.text: The position of how many letters will remain unchanged if each of the letters in the word ‘NIGHTMARES’ is re-arranged in the English alphabetical order from left to right?
questions.explanation: In alphabetical order NIGHTMARES becomes A E G H I M N R S T. Comparing position by position, G (3rd), H (4th), M (6th) and R (8th) stay where they were: four letters.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 5 – 4 ÷ 9 + 80 × 10 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 5 + 4 × 9 − 80 ÷ 10 = 5 + 36 − 8 = 33.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. (149, 213) (168, 232) (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In both pairs the second number is 64 more than the first (149 + 64 = 213, 168 + 64 = 232). Only (153, 217) follows the same rule.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. MEK: NVP :: GYT: TBG :: JWH:?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite letter in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on): M→N, E→V, K→P and G→T, Y→B, T→G. So J→Q, W→D, H→S, giving QDS.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No card is a parcel. All cards are envelopes. Some envelopes are bags. Conclusions: I. All envelopes can never be parcels. II. No card is a bag. III. At least some bags are postcards.
questions.explanation: Some envelopes are cards and no card is a parcel, so not every envelope can be a parcel: conclusion I follows. Nothing links cards and bags for certain (II), and postcards are not mentioned at all (III).

questions.text: Which of the four options will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? UE 88, VG 84, WI 80, XK76, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters run U, V, W, X, so next is Y; the second letters skip one each time (E, G, I, K), so next is M; the number falls by 4 (88, 84, 80, 76), so next is 72: YM72.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that when placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the letter series. L_P_QS_K_P_S_KP_Q_L_ _PQS
questions.explanation: Filling the blanks with K P L P Q L P S K P makes the block LKPPQS repeat four times: LKPPQS LKPPQS LKPPQS LKPPQS.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘what where how’ is written as ‘aa dd ff’; ‘where there that’ is written as ‘dd zz pp’ and ‘which what here’ is written as ‘ff kk ll’. How is ‘how’ written in that language?
questions.explanation: 'where' is common to the first two sentences and 'dd' to their codes, so where = dd; 'what' is common to the first and third, as is 'ff', so what = ff. The remaining word of the first sentence, 'how', is therefore 'aa'.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some tears are drops. Some drops are streams. All streams are rivers. Conclusions: I. All tears can never be rivers. II. Some drops are rivers. III. All tears being streams is a possibility.
options: Both II and III conclusion follow
Both I and II conclusion follow
questions.explanation: Some drops are streams and all streams are rivers, so some drops are rivers: II follows. No statement rules out every tear being a stream, so III is a possibility. I is not definite.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? YZUW, ?, QTQU, MQOT, INMS
questions.explanation: Letter by letter the terms move back by fixed steps: first letters −4 (Y, U, Q, M, I), second −3 (Z, W, T, Q, N), third −2 (U, S, Q, O, M) and fourth −1 (W, V, U, T, S). The missing term is UWSV.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’, ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the father of B’, ‘A $ B’ means ‘A is the son of B’, ‘A % B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’, ‘A / B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A = B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’. Which of the following means A is the daughter of K? i. A + K / J – P = D ii. J % P = K + A = D iii. K + A / P – D % J iv. D + K = A / P – J
questions.explanation: In K + A / P − D % J, 'K + A' means K is the mother of A, and 'A / P' means A is the wife of P, so A is female. A is therefore the daughter of K.

questions.text: 19 is related to 209 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 27 is related to 297. To which of the following is 61 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 11: 19 × 11 = 209 and 27 × 11 = 297, so 61 × 11 = 671.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 1, 3, 10, 41, ?, 1237
questions.explanation: Each term is the previous one multiplied by 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 in turn, plus 1: 1×2+1 = 3, 3×3+1 = 10, 10×4+1 = 41, 41×5+1 = 206 and 206×6+1 = 1237.

questions.text: In which year was Project Tiger launched in India?
questions.explanation: Project Tiger was launched by the Government of India in 1973 to conserve tigers and their habitat.

questions.text: Lathmar Holi is primarily celebrated in the state of:
questions.explanation: Lathmar Holi is celebrated in Barsana and Nandgaon in the Braj region of Uttar Pradesh.

questions.text: Which of the following awards was won by Lata Mangeshkar in the year 2001?
questions.explanation: Lata Mangeshkar was awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honour, in 2001.

questions.text: Details about Sudarshana lake is given in a rock inscription at Girnar (Junagarh), which was composed to record the achievements of the Shaka ruler _________.
questions.explanation: The Junagadh (Girnar) rock inscription of the Shaka ruler Rudradaman I records the repair of the Sudarshana lake and his achievements.

questions.text: ___________ is an industry association and self-regulatory organisation (SRO) whose primary objective is to work towards the robust development of the microfinance sector.
questions.explanation: Microfinance Institutions Network (MFIN) is the industry association of microfinance lenders that works as a self-regulatory organisation for the sector.

questions.text: Which article has a similar provision to that of Article 32 and deals with writ jurisdiction?
questions.explanation: Article 32 empowers the Supreme Court to issue writs; Article 226 gives the High Courts a similar, wider writ jurisdiction.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a condition for the President’s office in India?
options: He shall not hold any office of profit.
The allowances shall not be diminished during his term of office.
He shall not be entitled, without payment of rent, to use his official residence.
He shall not be a member of either House of the Parliament.
questions.explanation: Under Article 59 the President shall not be a member of either House or hold any office of profit, and his allowances shall not be diminished during his term; he is entitled to use his official residences without payment of rent. So the statement that he is not so entitled is not a condition.

questions.text: Which of the following statements best defines the monoecious?
options: A flower with both androecium and gynoecium
questions.explanation: In NCERT's usage 'monoecious' denotes the bisexual condition, with male and female reproductive structures together; of the options, that is a flower with both androecium and gynoecium.

questions.text: Mohan Veena player, Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt won the ____________ Award in the year 1994.
questions.explanation: Mohan Veena player Vishwa Mohan Bhatt won a Grammy Award in 1994 for the album 'A Meeting by the River', recorded with Ry Cooder.

questions.text: Who is Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology as of July 2023?
questions.explanation: In July 2023 Dr Jitendra Singh was Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology.

questions.text: Which of the following decomposition reactions is NOT a redox reaction?
questions.explanation: When calcium carbonate decomposes (CaCO3 → CaO + CO2), no element changes its oxidation state, so it is not a redox reaction; the other three decompositions involve oxidation and reduction.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following has authored the play ‘Nil Darpan’?
questions.explanation: Nil Darpan, a Bengali play on the oppression of indigo cultivators, was written by Dinabandhu Mitra.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following formed the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha in 1929?
questions.explanation: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati founded the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha in 1929.

questions.text: Which plateaus are very fertile because they are rich in black soil that is very good for farming?
questions.explanation: The Deccan lava (trap) plateau is covered with black soil formed from basalt, which holds moisture and is very fertile.

questions.text: Which of the following is a correct order of basicity?
questions.explanation: Down the alkali-metal group (Li, Na, K, Cs) the hydroxides become more strongly basic, so CsOH > KOH > NaOH > LiOH.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECT regarding the grade of organisation and its example?
questions.explanation: Paramecium (protoplasmic grade), Sycon (cellular grade) and jellyfish (cell-tissue grade) are correctly paired. Euplectella is a sponge, of the cellular grade, so pairing it with the tissue-organ grade is incorrect.

questions.text: The head office of Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is located in ________.
questions.explanation: The head office of the Board of Control for Cricket in India is in Mumbai.

questions.text: When the analysis of population density is done by calculating it through net cultivated area, then the measure is termed as:
questions.explanation: Physiological density is the total population divided by the net cultivated area.

questions.text: Mahendravarman I was the ruler of which of the following dynasties?
questions.explanation: Mahendravarman I was a ruler of the Pallava dynasty of Kanchipuram.

questions.text: What challenge does foreign investment often face in India?
questions.explanation: SSC's answer is an inconsistent regulatory environment: rules and approvals that keep changing make long-term foreign investment uncertain.

questions.text: Which of the following states is the biggest producer of Pulses?
questions.explanation: Of the states listed, Madhya Pradesh is by far the largest producer of pulses.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who founded the Prarthana Samaj in Mumbai in 1867?
questions.explanation: The Prarthana Samaj was founded in Bombay in 1867 by Atmaram Pandurang.

questions.text: Who is the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu as of July 2023?
questions.explanation: M.K. Stalin has been Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu since May 2021, so he held the office in July 2023.

questions.text: In which city was the first golf club of India situated?
questions.explanation: The Royal Calcutta Golf Club, founded in Kolkata in 1829, was India's first golf club.

questions.text: Which Indian among the following has his name in Time Magazine’s list of ‘100 most influential people of 2021’?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi was among the Indians on Time magazine's list of the 100 most influential people of 2021.

questions.text: A grocer professes to sell rice at the cost price, but uses a fake weight of 870 g for 1 kg. Find his profit percentage (correct to two decimal places).
questions.explanation: He gives 870 g but charges for 1000 g, so his profit is 130/870 × 100 ≈ 14.94%.

questions.text: In a circular race of 840 m, A and B start running in the same direction at the same time from the same point at the speeds of 6 m/s and 12 m/s, respectively. After how much time will they meet next?
questions.explanation: Running in the same direction, B gains 12 − 6 = 6 m/s on A. They meet again when B has gained one full lap: 840 ÷ 6 = 140 s.

questions.text: Let O be the centre of the circle and AB and CD are two parallel chords on the same side of the radius. OP is perpendicular to AB and OQ is perpendicular to CD. If AB = 10 cm, CD = 24 cm and PQ = 7 cm, then the diameter (in cm) of the circle is equal to:
questions.explanation: The half-chords are 5 cm and 12 cm. With radius r, OP = √(r² − 25) and OQ = √(r² − 144), and with both chords on the same side OP − OQ = 7. r = 13 fits (12 − 5 = 7), so the diameter is 26 cm.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is sufficient to conclude that two triangles are congruent?
options: One side and one angle of both triangles are equal.
These have two equal sides and the same perimeter.
These have the same area and the same base.
These have the same base and the same height.
questions.explanation: If two sides are equal and the perimeters are equal, the third sides are equal too, so the triangles are congruent by SSS. None of the other conditions fixes all three sides.

questions.text: Fill pipe P is 21 times faster than fill pipe Q. If Q can fill a cistern in 110 minutes, find the time it takes to fill the cistern when both fill pipes are opened together.
questions.explanation: Q fills 1/110 of the cistern a minute and P, 21 times faster, fills 21/110. Together they fill 22/110 = 1/5 a minute, so they take 5 minutes.

questions.text: R pays ₹100 to P with ₹5, ₹2 and ₹1 coins. The total number of coins used for paying are 40. What is the number of coins of denomination ₹5 in the payment?
questions.explanation: With a coins of ₹5, b of ₹2 and c of ₹1: 5a + 2b + c = 100 and a + b + c = 40, so 4a + b = 60 and a cannot exceed 15. Of the options only 13 works (b = 8, c = 19).

questions.text: The radii of the two cones are in the ratio of 2 : 5 and their volumes are in the ratio of 3 : 5. What is the ratio of their heights?
questions.explanation: Volume = (1/3)πr²h, so height is proportional to V/r². Ratio of heights = (3/5) ÷ (4/25) = (3/5) × (25/4) = 15 : 4.

questions.text: Which of the following can be the value of ‘k’ so that the number 217924k is divisible by 6?
questions.explanation: For divisibility by 6 the number must be even and its digit sum divisible by 3. 2 + 1 + 7 + 9 + 2 + 4 = 25, so k must be 2, 5 or 8, and even: of the options, 2.

questions.text: In an election between two candidates, y% of the voters did not vote. 10% of the votes cast were declared invalid, while all the valid votes were cast in favour of either of the two candidates. The candidate who got 59.375% of the valid votes cast was declared elected by 2484 votes. If the number of people eligible to vote in that election was 16,000, what is the value of y?
questions.explanation: The winner's margin is 59.375% − 40.625% = 18.75% of valid votes = 2484, so there were 13,248 valid votes. These are 90% of the votes cast, so 14,720 people voted out of 16,000, i.e. 92%. So y = 8.

questions.text: An article is marked at ₹550. If it is sold at a discount of 40%, then the selling price becomes 10% more than its cost price. What is the cost price (in ₹)?
questions.explanation: Selling price = 60% of ₹550 = ₹330, which is 110% of the cost price, so CP = 330 ÷ 1.1 = ₹300.

questions.text: If the sum of two sides of an equilateral triangle is 16 cm, then find the third side.
questions.explanation: All sides of an equilateral triangle are equal. Two sides total 16 cm, so each side, including the third, is 8 cm.

questions.text: The distance between the centres of two circles of radii 22 cm and 10 cm is 37 cm. If the points of contact of a direct common tangent to these circles are M and Q, then find the length of the line segment MQ.
questions.explanation: Length of a direct common tangent = √(d² − (r₁ − r₂)²) = √(37² − 12²) = √(1369 − 144) = √1225 = 35 cm.

questions.text: The average marks (out of 100) of boys and girls in an examination are 75 and 80, respectively. If the average marks of all the students in that examination are 78. Find the ratio of the number of boys to the number of girls.
questions.explanation: By alligation, boys : girls = (80 − 78) : (78 − 75) = 2 : 3.

questions.text: Mohan borrows a sum of ₹4,22,092 at the rate of 20% per annum simple interest. At the end of the first year, he repays ₹21,679 towards return of principal amount borrowed. If Mohan clears all pending dues at the end of the second year, including interest payment that accrued during the first year, how much does he pay (in ₹) at the end of the second year?
questions.explanation: First-year interest = 20% of ₹4,22,092 = ₹84,418.40. After repaying ₹21,679 of principal, ₹4,00,413 remains, earning ₹80,082.60 in the second year. At the end of year two he pays 4,00,413 + 84,418.40 + 80,082.60 = ₹5,64,914.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Fatal
questions.explanation: 'Fatal' means causing death: 'deadly'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. Lovely tunes are composed by Domnica.
questions.explanation: 'Are composed by Domnica' is simple present passive, so the active is 'Domnica composes lovely tunes', with the adjective before the noun.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the opposite meaning of the underlined word. The explosive used is of my own formulation, and I can “vouch” for its efficiency.
questions.explanation: To 'vouch' for something is to confirm or guarantee it; the opposite is 'invalidate'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. Mr. Abhilash and his family / have received / no informations / about the incident.
questions.explanation: 'Information' is uncountable and has no plural, so it should be 'no information'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Toxic
questions.explanation: 'Toxic' means poisonous or deadly: 'lethal'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Unit of weight for precious stones
questions.explanation: The carat is the unit of weight for precious stones.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. She is “proficient in speaking many languages”.
questions.explanation: Someone proficient in many languages is 'multilingual'; 'bilingual' means two languages.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Ishika saw the tiger in the forest.
options: The tiger saw by Ishika in the forest.
The tiger sees Ishika in the forest.
The tiger was seen by Ishika in the forest.
The tiger was seen by the forest in Ishika.
questions.explanation: Simple past active 'saw the tiger' becomes 'was seen': 'The tiger was seen by Ishika in the forest.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who likes to argue about anything
questions.explanation: A 'contentious' person is one given to arguing.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. ‘Spy Family’ is a graphic novel that is a narrative work in which the story is conveyed to the reader using “uninterrupted art in a traditional” comics format.
questions.explanation: A graphic novel tells its story through art panels arranged in sequence, i.e. 'sequential art'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. My brother performed / extremely good / in the class test / held yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Performed' needs an adverb: 'extremely well', not 'extremely good'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'relevant'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym to replace the underlined word in the given sentence. No “altruistic” act is truly sincere.
questions.explanation: 'Altruistic' means unselfishly concerned for the good of others: 'philanthropic'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Innuendo
questions.explanation: An 'innuendo' is an indirect hint, usually an unpleasant one: an 'insinuation'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Vinod had a ________ escape in the car accident.
questions.explanation: 'A narrow escape' is the fixed expression for only just avoiding danger.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given phrase. A short interesting story about a real person or event
questions.explanation: An 'anecdote' is a short, interesting story about a real person or incident.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To have bigger fish to fry
options: To have bigger things to take care of than the menial task at hand
To know different kinds of fishing techniques
To have an interest in cooking
questions.explanation: 'To have bigger fish to fry' means to have more important matters to deal with.

questions.text: In the following sentence, four words are underlined out of which one word is misspelt. Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word. After the recapture (A) of Tololing and the adjacent features, evacting (B) the enemy from this well-fortified (C) position became a priority.(D)
questions.explanation: (B) is misspelt: the word is 'evicting'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. She has been “studying for two o’clock” .
questions.explanation: With a point in time ('two o'clock') the present perfect continuous takes 'since'; 'for' goes with a period of time.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. There is a saying that coming events cast their shadows before. (1)________, it is not universally true. Something can happen within a second, and one may not (2)________ it. (3)________, some instances show that predictions based on certain signs have gone wrong. People generally say that natural calamities can be predicted by observing the animals. But what if animals are suffering from some disease and don’t show any signs before the event appears? They may fail to make peculiar sounds or actions about the events which are going to take place. (4)________, some unnatural calamities that are likely to appear may forecast their shadows by some bad omens. (5)________, we should not completely cancel out the possibilities that animals can sense certain unnatural happenings.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The sentence qualifies the saying before it, so a contrast word is needed: 'However'.
